current.text: He joined the Lakers from Utah and is locked in as their starting center. The Lakers' defense depends heavily on him.
His backups at center are weak. Kevon Looney is the listed backup, and Mamukelashvili may take those minutes.
With weak backups behind him, he is expected to play heavy minutes.
Expected line this season: about 12 to 15 points, with around six from offensive rebounds, double-digit rebounds, 2+ blocks and bad free throws.
Andy expects Luka Doncic to make him look very good as a roller and dunking threat.
His threes and high steal rate came from a five-game sample, and the experts expect both to drop this season. That also lowers his FG% and scoring a little.
Josh says managers should not avoid him because he missed most of last season. He thinks Kessler might play 80 games.
His Yahoo price is too high. The experts call a rank in the 20s or 30s, a top 30 pick or round 3 an overdraft and fade him there. Pick 42 is better but still not loved.
At an ESPN ADP around 80 he is a fair, easy pick.
Josh would not pay more than 15 USD in an auction. Others value him more, and he went for 26 USD in an auction mock.
His draft spot in mocks varies a lot, from early round 3 to late round 4.
He is a very good pick for a team that is low on rebounds.

durable.text: He is a three-category center: rebounds, FG% and blocks. His free throws are poor, and his assists, steals, threes and points give little.
The experts see him as a very one-dimensional player. Nothing outside his three strong categories is good, and much of it is bad.
An elite rim protector and defensive rebounder.
His career three-point percentage is 20 to 25%. His steal rate was very low before last season's five games.
He has had arm or shoulder problems in two of the last three seasons, including shoulder surgery last season.
Because of these arm and shoulder injuries, it is unclear how many minutes his body can handle.

note: Kessler is a strong three-category center: blocks (z +4.3), rebounds (+3.0) and FG% (+2.5). His FT% is a clear liability (-2.8), so he fits punt FT builds best. Yahoo values him at 24 USD (average cost 18.8) and ESPN at 13 USD (8.4). He went for 15 USD in our league last season. The experts say about 15 USD is his ceiling, and a 26 USD price like the one in an auction mock is an overpay. Early in the season, check whether his three-point attempts and steals hold up, and whether his shoulder lets him play full starter minutes.
